passage:
Subject: finally some good news!!

Uma,
You know how stressed I've been about the semester fee. Papa's shop had a bad month and I didn't want to ask him again.
Well, today I got a message from an HR officer at an online marketing company. Super polite. She said my profile 'stood out' and they have a work-from-home job: rating products, two hours a day, ₹3,000 a week. She even had a proper-looking logo and a company address in Gurugram. She said the spots are filling fast and I need to reply by tonight.
I've never even applied there. But she explained they find students through college lists. That makes sense, right?
She was so friendly. She asked about my course and said she has a cousin in the same college.
I'll tell you more tomorrow. I feel like things are finally turning.
Pankaj

qa.q: How much did the message say the job pays per week?
qa.a: It said ₹3,000 a week.

qa.q: Why is Pankaj so excited about the message?
qa.a: Pankaj is worried about the semester fee and doesn't want to ask Papa again, so a friendly, flattering offer feels like relief.

qa.q: What should Pankaj do before replying by tonight?
qa.a: Pankaj should pause, look up the company's official contact details separately and check with Uma or a trusted adult, because an urgent offer for a job never applied for is a warning sign.

qa.q: How might Uma feel reading this email?
qa.a: Uma may be happy for Pankaj but also uneasy about the tight deadline and the job that came without an application.

grounding: It shows a spoof job offer arriving at a moment of money need, friendly and urgent, appearing to come from a real company.

passage:
Parveen, you asked why I'm smiling at my phone. Okay, don't laugh.
So you know how it's been since I moved here for college. Nobody talks to me in the hostel. I eat alone most nights. Weekends are the worst.
Then three weeks ago someone messaged me on the photo app. Her name's Zara, she says she's a medical student in Dubai. She liked my photo of the old fort and said I have 'an artist's eye'. Nobody's ever said that to me.
Now we talk every night. She remembers everything, my exam dates, my roommate's snoring. She sends voice notes. She says she's never met anyone who listens like me.
She hasn't asked for anything. She says she wants to video call soon but her camera's broken.
I know, I know. But Parveen, she makes me feel like I matter here.
I'm Imran, the guy nobody noticed. And someone noticed.

qa.q: How long ago did the first message arrive?
qa.a: Three weeks ago.

qa.q: What is Imran feeling that makes Zara's messages so powerful?
qa.a: Imran feels lonely and unnoticed in the hostel, so being praised and remembered makes him feel he matters.

qa.q: What could Parveen gently suggest to Imran at this stage?
qa.a: Parveen could suggest that Imran keep personal details private, not send money or photos, and be cautious that the video call keeps being delayed, while talking to someone he trusts.

qa.q: What is it like for Parveen to hear Imran say he feels unnoticed?
qa.a: Parveen may feel sad and protective, realising how lonely he has been, and worried about the stranger filling that gap.

grounding: It shows an online admirer approaching a lonely young man at a moment of need, friendly and flattering, the approach seeming real and warm.

passage:
The message came the week after my third job rejection, when hostel fees were due and Appa had just said, carefully, that money was tight this month.
"Hello Shankar! We loved your profile. Work-from-home data role, great salary, no interview needed. Reply YES to receive your offer letter. Only 3 seats left!" It was signed Ms Kapoor, HR, with a smiling photo and a company name that sounded real.
I read it maybe twenty times. It felt like the universe had finally noticed me. No interview. Somebody had loved my profile.
I typed YES. My thumb hovered over send.
Dilnaz, my roommate, looked over my shoulder. "Since when do companies love a profile without meeting you?" she said. "And why the rush?"
I laughed it off. But I didn't press send. Not yet.

qa.q: How many seats did the message say were left?
qa.a: Only 3 seats left.

qa.q: Why did the message feel like the universe had noticed Shankar?
qa.a: Shankar felt rejected and anxious about fees, so the warm, easy offer felt like relief and recognition.

qa.q: What could Shankar do before pressing send?
qa.a: Pause, look up the company's official website and number independently, and check with Dilnaz or the college placement cell.

qa.q: What might Dilnaz be noticing that Shankar isn't?
qa.a: Dilnaz sees the warning signs, praise without a meeting and a rush, and feels uneasy for her roommate.

grounding: A friendly, urgent fake job offer arrives just when a young adult feels rejected and short of money, appearing to come from a real company.

passage:
Hostel warden's note, 7 August
At about 4 p.m. I found Harsha in the hostel lobby on a call, pacing and pale. Sangeeta, a friend from the same floor, stood beside him looking worried. The caller claimed to be from a courier company: a parcel from abroad was held in customs under Harsha's name, and a "clearance fee" had to be paid within the hour or the police would be informed.
Harsha told me later he had been waiting for a birthday parcel from his brother in Dubai, so it sounded real.
I asked him to put the call on hold. We checked the courier company's official website together; its number was different. When we called it, they had no such parcel.
Harsha was shaken and embarrassed. I told him scammers target exactly this kind of moment and that asking for help was right. We reported the number to the cyber-crime helpline together.

qa.q: What did the caller say was held in customs?
qa.a: A parcel from abroad under Harsha's name.

qa.q: What was Harsha feeling during the call?
qa.a: He felt panicked and pressured, pale and pacing, because he really was waiting for a parcel.

qa.q: What did the warden do that others could copy?
qa.a: Put the call on hold, found the official number independently, confirmed there was no parcel, and reported the caller.

qa.q: What might Sangeeta have felt standing beside Harsha?
qa.a: Sangeeta likely felt worried and unsure how to help, then relieved when the warden stepped in.

grounding: A warden notes how an urgent fake courier call reached a student at a moment of real expectation, seeming to come from a courier and customs.

passage:
Sunday night
Four months in Chennai and I still eat dinner alone most nights. Today a message came from a stranger on the photo app: "Your pictures of the beach are beautiful. You see the world like a poet." His name is Arvind; he says he's an engineer on a ship, travelling. We talked for three hours. He asked about my day, remembered the name of my cat back home, and said he had never met anyone so easy to talk to.
I felt warm all evening, as if someone had switched on a lamp in my room.
Ganga aunty, my landlady, asked why I was smiling at my phone. I didn't tell her. I don't know why. It's probably nothing. He says he'll call tomorrow from the ship.
I'm going to sleep with the phone near my pillow.
Vandana

qa.q: What job does Arvind say he has?
qa.a: An engineer on a ship.

qa.q: How did Vandana feel after talking to Arvind for three hours?
qa.a: Vandana felt warm and less lonely, as if someone had switched on a lamp in the room.

qa.q: What could help Vandana before the next call?
qa.a: Telling Ganga aunty or a friend about Arvind, and being cautious if he ever asks for money, secrecy or personal details, never sending any.

qa.q: What might Ganga aunty sense when she sees Vandana smiling?
qa.a: Ganga aunty may feel glad Vandana seems happier, but curious and a little protective about the cause.

grounding: A lonely young adult receives a flattering message from a so-called admirer abroad, a friendly approach arriving at a moment of need.

passage:
[Monday, 11:30 pm]
Unknown: Hi Rehana! 😊 Your profile was shortlisted for part-time online work. Rs 800 per task, 1 hour daily. Interested?
Rehana: how did you get my number?
Unknown: From the job portal, dear. You look very talented. Only 5 seats left, reply fast
[Rehana switches to another chat]
Rehana: Jasleen are u up
Jasleen: ya, why?
Rehana: some HR person messaged about online work. hostel fee is due Friday and papa's shop has been slow
Rehana: 800 per task. that's like the whole fee in a week
Jasleen: which company?
Rehana: didn't say. but they know my name and my college
Jasleen: hmm
Rehana: they said only 5 seats. should I reply before morning?
Jasleen: sleep first? we can look it up tomorrow
Rehana: ok but what if the seats go 😔

qa.q: When is Rehana's hostel fee due?
qa.a: Rehana's hostel fee is due Friday.

qa.q: Why is Rehana tempted to reply before morning?
qa.a: Rehana is anxious about the hostel fee and her papa's slow shop, so the friendly offer and the only-5-seats warning make her hopeful and rushed.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Rehana right now?
qa.a: Rehana could follow Jasleen's idea, wait until morning, and check the company through an official source or the college placement cell before replying.

qa.q: How might Jasleen feel reading these messages late at night?
qa.a: Jasleen may feel uneasy and protective, noticing the missing company name and the rush, while trying not to make Rehana feel foolish.

grounding: Shows a friendly, urgent job offer from a stranger arriving at a moment of need, when a fee is due and money is tight.
